creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Mercado Libre (MELI) and Sea Limited (SE) head to head as both face investor pessimism over rising delivery costs, consumer pressure and potential defaults. Wall Street expects MELI to grow earnings per share by 28% a year over the next several years, ahead of SE at 18.5%. MELI recently lowered its free-shipping threshold, reinvigorating customer growth but pressuring margins: its operating margin is 7.4% and declining, and return on invested capital is 7.8% and falling, as management prioritises growth over profitability. SE, which runs e-commerce, financial services and gaming — gaming being the highest-margin segment, though e-commerce and financial services are growing faster — has a 7.8% operating margin that is improving dramatically, and ROIC of 11% and rising, partly by renting rather than owning logistics assets. On valuation, MELI trades at 27x forward earnings versus SE at 14.6x. His discounted cash flow model values SE at $104 against a $70 market price, near its 52-week low, so SE looks undervalued; MELI also looks undervalued, though the caption garbles the passage and omits both his MELI fair-value figure and its current price. He ranks both as buying opportunities, but if forced to pick one he would choose MELI. Calls: MELI BUY, SE BUY at about $70.
